ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The bottom of the circuit is a common wire, which may be chosen as the reference ground. On the left is an independent voltage source V, with polarity positive at the upper terminal and negative at the lower terminal; its upper terminal is connected to the 3Ω resistor on the upper left. The right end of the 3Ω resistor is connected in series to a 0.2H horizontal inductor, and this inductor is labeled with voltage V_x, with polarity left positive and right negative. The right end of the horizontal inductor forms the central upper node, and this node is connected downward through a 0.5H inductor to the reference ground, with current I_1 labeled as downward. The central upper node is also connected rightward through a 5Ω resistor to the upper terminal of the dependent voltage source on the right; the dependent source is labeled 0.2V_x, with polarity in the figure negative at the upper terminal and positive at the lower terminal, and the lower terminal is connected to the reference ground. Reasoning: Let the central upper node voltage be v_n, and the bottom reference ground voltage be 0. Since the current I_1 of the 0.5H inductor is downward and enters its upper terminal, according to the passive sign convention there is v_n = 0.5 dI_1/dt. Define the current i in the upper-left series branch as flowing from left to right. The voltage at the upper terminal of the left voltage source is V, and after passing through the 3Ω resistor and V_x labeled left positive and right negative, it reaches the central node, so V - 3i - V_x = v_n, that is, i = (V - V_x - v_n)/3. The lower terminal of the right dependent source is grounded and is the positive terminal, while the upper terminal is the negative terminal, so its upper terminal node voltage is -0.2V_x. Therefore the current in the 5Ω resistor flowing from the central node to the right node is (v_n - (-0.2V_x))/5 = (v_n + 0.2V_x)/5. Write KCL at the central node: the current flowing in from the left branch is equal to the sum of the downward inductor current and the rightward resistor current: i = I_1 + (v_n + 0.2V_x)/5. Substituting v_n = 0.5 dI_1/dt gives (V - V_x - 0.5 dI_1/dt)/3 = I_1 + (0.5 dI_1/dt + 0.2V_x)/5. Multiplying both sides by 15 and arranging: 5V - 5V_x - 2.5 dI_1/dt = 15I_1 + 1.5 dI_1/dt + 0.6V_x, so 4 dI_1/dt = 5V - 5.6V_x - 15I_1. Finally obtain dI_1/dt = -1.4V_x - 3.75I_1 + 5V/4.

method.method_draft: First describe the image-derived circuit and choose the bottom wire as reference. Let the central top node voltage be \(v_n\). From the vertical \(0.5\text{ H}\) inductor with current \(I_1\) downward, write \(v_n=0.5\,dI_1/dt\). Define the current through the left top series branch from left to right as \(i\). Using the left source, the \(3\Omega\) resistor, and the horizontal inductor voltage \(V_x\), write \(i=(V-V_x-v_n)/3\). From the dependent source polarity in the image, the right node above the source is \(-0.2V_x\), so the current through the \(5\Omega\) resistor from the central node to the right is \((v_n+0.2V_x)/5\). Apply KCL at the central node: \(i=I_1+(v_n+0.2V_x)/5\). Substitute \(v_n=0.5\,dI_1/dt\) and solve algebraically for \(dI_1/dt\), giving \(dI_1/dt=-1.4V_x-3.75I_1+\frac{5}{4}V\).
